rationale: D1, data-informed (not zero-shot): the first candidate of the clock spec for normal flames. The train table shows what the generic hazard surface of the first generation could not hold: self-extinction is radiative and its time diverges as the fuel flow falls towards the flow a flame can hold (about 0.7 mg/s in 39 % O2), with a floor of about 6 s while the flame establishes; below that flow the test ends on the burner temperature limit, sooner the lower the flow; flames with T_ad below about 1750 K go out within a second or two; and a few tests end at script durations. Numbers typed from the train table by the author; no fit, no search.
